projects.title: From ECG images to diagnostic language
projects.contributors: Elijah Rockers, Sadeer Al-Kindi, and a multidisciplinary collaboration led by Rohan Khera.
projects.summary: ECG-GPT generates diagnostic text from 12-lead ECG images, with evaluation across multiple countries.
projects.problem: ECGs are often shared as images. Computational interpretation must work across different recording and presentation settings.
projects.approach: A vision-to-language model was developed using ECG recordings paired with cardiologist-confirmed diagnostic statements.
projects.finding: The study reports development and multinational validation of image-based ECG interpretation.
projects.question: How can image-based interpretation be evaluated and integrated responsibly into clinical workflows?

projects.title: More information from a calcium scan
projects.contributors: Khurram Nasir and collaborators in the AI-CVD initiative.
projects.summary: AI-derived cardiac chamber ratios from coronary calcium scans were associated with future heart failure.
projects.problem: A coronary calcium scan contains anatomical information beyond the calcium score.
projects.approach: Investigators evaluated automated left-to-right cardiac chamber volume ratios in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
projects.finding: Cardiac chamber volume ratios provided prognostic information about incident heart failure.
projects.question: Can opportunistic measurements support earlier identification of people who need further assessment?

projects.title: A window into cardiovascular risk
projects.contributors: Sadeer Al-Kindi, Rohan Dhamdhere, Gourav Modanwal, Anant Madabhushi, and CRIC collaborators.
projects.summary: Retinal vascular features helped stratify cardiovascular risk in people with chronic kidney disease.
projects.problem: People with chronic kidney disease have heterogeneous cardiovascular risk. Retinal images offer a noninvasive view of the microvasculature.
projects.approach: The CARE-CKD study used deep learning to segment retinal vessels and machine learning to evaluate vascular features alongside clinical markers.
projects.finding: Retinal features added information for cardiovascular risk assessment in the CRIC cohort.
projects.question: How well do these features generalize to other populations and prospective clinical settings?

projects.title: Transportation noise and metabolic health
projects.contributors: Jad Ardakani, Izza Shahid, Rakesh Gullapelli, Khurram Nasir, Sadeer Al-Kindi, and collaborators.
projects.summary: A retrospective study examines transportation noise exposure and the development of type 2 diabetes.
projects.problem: The environments in which people live may influence cardiometabolic health.
projects.approach: The study linked transportation noise exposure with incident diabetes in an observational analysis.
projects.finding: This publication examines the association between transportation noise and type 2 diabetes; the paper provides the estimates and methodological details.
projects.question: Which environmental factors may inform prevention strategies at the population level?

projects.title: Biological aging from routine blood tests
projects.contributors: Adi Siddharth, Budhaditya Bose, Rakesh Gullapelli, Charlie Nicolas, Khurram Nasir, Sadeer Al-Kindi, and collaborators.
projects.summary: HemeAge explores machine learning measures of hematologic aging and cardiovascular risk in two cohorts.
projects.problem: Routine blood tests may contain information about biological aging that is not captured by chronological age alone.
projects.approach: Investigators used machine learning to examine hematologic biomarkers of aging in relation to cardiovascular risk.
projects.finding: The publication evaluates HemeAge and cardiovascular risk across two cohorts.
projects.question: Can biomarkers derived from routine tests improve scalable risk assessment?

projects.title: The environment across the heart failure journey
projects.contributors: Sadeer Al-Kindi with Omar Hahad, Sanjay Rajagopalan, and collaborators.
projects.summary: A research review connects environmental exposures with heart failure risk and progression.
projects.problem: Heart failure develops within a broader environmental and social context.
projects.approach: This review synthesizes evidence on the environmental exposome across heart failure risk and progression.
projects.finding: The publication brings environmental exposures into the discussion of heart failure prevention and disease progression.
projects.question: How can exposure assessment inform future mechanistic and prevention studies?
